protocol.py: 11 biology problems (3 errors, 4 warnings, 4 notes).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: tube D1 in slot 2
   line 35:  p300_multi.aspirate(50, mix_well)
   At line 35 the tip went into tube D1 in slot 2 while it still carried mix (tube A1 in
   slot 2), template 1 (tube B1 in slot 2) and template 5 (tube C1 in slot 2) from an
   earlier step (this line did it 3 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a
   little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does
   not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted material along into 2 other
   wells: wells C1 and D1 in slot 3.
   Affected: tube D1 in slot 2.
   Also reached 2 other wells: wells C1 and D1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 35 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [bb14040a2c23]

           https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opentrons/opentrons/edge/shared-data/labware/schemas/2.json

5. WARNING ENZYME-BEFORE-DILUENT: An enzyme was added before the water: mix
   line 36:  p300_multi.dispense(50, dw)
   At line 36 the robot put mix into wells C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3 (this line
   did it twice). Take well D1 in slot 3: at that moment it was dry, and the water came
   afterwards, at line 45, to make the 42 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An
   enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction,
   after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into
   neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme
   then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed
   template.
   Affected: wells C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to wells C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3: water and buffer
   first, then the sample, then mix last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme
   in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.

   component)

   still carried template 1 (tube B1 in slot 2) and template 5 (tube C1 in slot 2) from an
   earlier step (this line did it 5 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a

findings.explanation: At line 44 the tip went into water (tube A2 in slot 2) and tube D2 in slot 2 while it still carried mix (tube A1 in slot 2), water (tube A2 in slot 2), template 2 (tube B2 in slot 2), template 6 (tube C2 in slot 2) and 1 more from an earlier step (this line did it 4 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from them then took the unwanted material along into 1 other well: well B1 in slot 3.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 44 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: More liquid than the well can hold: 284 ul in a 217 ul well, 5 wells
findings.explanation: At line 45 the robot filled wells B1, C1, E1, G1 and H1 in slot 3 past the rim (217 ul to the rim by the labware definition's shape; the maker states 100 ul) (this line did it 5 times), reaching 284 ul. The liquid runs into the neighbouring wells and onto the deck; the volumes still add up on paper, so the plate map does not see it, and the simulator says nothing. Wells: wells B1, C1, E1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
findings.fix: Use labware with bigger wells, or scale every volume down so the fullest well stays under the stated maximum with room to mix.

findings.title: A used tip carried template 1 (tube B1 in slot 2) and template 5 (tube C1 in slot 2) into 5 wells it was never meant for
findings.explanation: At line 36 the tip touched the liquid in wells D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3 while it still carried template 1 (tube B1 in slot 2) and template 5 (tube C1 in slot 2) from an earlier step (this line did it 5 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into these wells on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different samples, each now holds a little of another.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 36. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is already in the well.

findings.title: An enzyme was added before the water: mix
findings.explanation: At line 36 the robot put mix into wells C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3 (this line did it twice). Take well D1 in slot 3: at that moment it was dry, and the water came afterwards, at line 45, to make the 42 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
findings.fix: Reorder the additions to wells C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3: water and buffer first, then the sample, then mix last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.

findings.title: More liquid than the well is rated for: 192 ul against 100 ul, 2 wells
findings.explanation: At line 45 the robot filled wells D1 and F1 in slot 3 past the 100 ul the maker states for it (this line did it twice), reaching 192 ul, under the 217 ul the well holds to its rim. Above the stated maximum the liquid climbs the wall and wets the seal, a tip going in displaces it over the edge, and the volumes still add up on paper, so the plate map does not see it and the simulator says nothing. Wells: wells D1 and F1 in slot 3.
findings.fix: Use labware rated for the volume, or scale every volume down so the fullest well stays under the stated maximum with room to mix.

findings.title: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a reagent
findings.explanation: At line 36 the tip touched the liquid in wells D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3 while it still carried template 1 (tube B1 in slot 2) and template 5 (tube C1 in slot 2) from an earlier step (this line did it 5 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, and the protocol never transfers that liquid into these wells on purpose. A reagent is shared: the master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every reaction on the plate. A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a no-template control can no longer be trusted.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 36, or add the reagent to the wells first, while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: 3 wells never mixed after water and the liquid from tube D2 in slot 2 went in (19 to 23% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 45 the robot added water and the liquid from tube D2 in slot 2 to wells B1, E1 and F1 in slot 3, which already held mix, template 5, the liquid from tube D1 in slot 2, template 6 and 1 more (this line did it 3 times). The addition was 19 to 23% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
findings.fix: Mix wells B1, E1 and F1 in slot 3 after line 45: `mix_after=(5, 147 to 205)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 147 to 205, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
